endorsements.quote: Co-design tools with end users, including patients and providers, to ensure cultural relevance and build trust.

unlisted_practices: Prioritise AI diagnostic tools that work offline, are robust in low-resource settings, and match local epidemiology and clinical workflows.
Prioritise edge AI (locally implemented offline diagnostic systems) over cloud-based solutions for AI diagnostics in low-connectivity settings.
Train and support healthcare workers to integrate AI tools into routine care, with clear referral and treatment protocols.
Strengthen local laboratory capacity through personnel training and clear quality assurance protocols.
Establish regulatory frameworks, screening policies, and adaptive evaluation pathways that enable safe and equitable adoption of AI diagnostics in LMICs.

Create sustainable financing models such as pooled procurement, insurance coverage, reimbursement mechanisms, and public-private partnerships that cover full implementation costs including maintenance and training.
Embed AI-supported diagnostic methods into national disease control programmes.
Raise community awareness of diseases diagnosable with AI-based methods to build trust and uptake.
Ensure human oversight, adherence to existing regulations, and continuous monitoring during AI diagnostic implementation.
Integrate AI diagnostic tools into healthcare pathways that link diagnosis to timely treatment and referral.
Expand pilot regional AI programmes when proved effective.

screen.reason: Commentary/analysis examining how AI could be applied to diagnostic methods in global women's health in resource-limited settings.
